stage.title: Freeze canonical format and delete conflicting public paths

goal: Lock the long-term canonical profiler format, freeze the normalized time contract, make the delete list explicit, and keep implementation aligned while the first consumer migration slices land.

execution_status.current_focus: CP-03 repository-wide deletion follow-through after the consumer boundary landed
recently_landed: ProfileDump event_type is now part of the canonical schema contract and tests use event_type-based lookup.
Canonical timing template declarations were extracted into profile/ProfileDumpTemplates.h for shared producer and consumer use.
MoerProfiler now has a canonical ProfileDump TCP/file consumer path with event_type dispatch for CPU and GPU scope records.
MoerProfiler consumer storage no longer depends on trace/Trace.h types and now uses local consumer-owned session/event/track structures.
The shared source/profiler/ProfileSession module now owns decoder state and session-relative normalization for both the profiler app and focused tests.
Focused regression now includes profiler-side file-load normalization and incremental stream normalization checks.
remaining_before_m1_exit: Remove the remaining repository-wide legacy public profiler surfaces, especially source/profile as a public subsystem and the old Trace transport role outside the canonical consumer path.
Decide whether canonical session metadata must be emitted explicitly instead of using first-event origin inference in the consumer.
Keep the checkpoint text aligned with the now-landed shared ProfileSession module instead of the previous main.cpp-local implementation.

parallel_contracts.name: Trace packet transport
parallel_contracts.detail: MoerProfiler live ingest currently consumes Trace metadata and event packets directly over TCP.

parallel_contracts.name: ProfileDump packet transport
parallel_contracts.detail: A schema-driven binary file and TCP stream already exists and already has focused parser tests.

parallel_contracts.name: Trace CSV offline path
parallel_contracts.detail: MoerProfiler still has a CSV load workflow, which duplicates offline parsing logic and keeps a second storage contract alive.

parallel_contracts.name: source/profile legacy public path
parallel_contracts.detail: The old module still exists as a separate public profiler surface even though its Save path is already forwarding into ProfileDump.

time_model_problem.detail: Trace uses raw steady_clock nanoseconds and preserves them through serialization.
Profiler UI currently stores and renders raw event timestamps directly instead of freezing one canonical normalized session time model.

hard_constraints.title: Stage 1 is planning-only but binding
hard_constraints.detail: This stage does not implement code yet, but it must freeze format, time, and deletion rules so later stages do not reopen them casually.

hard_constraints.title: No compatibility language
hard_constraints.detail: Do not phrase Trace packet transport, CSV, or source/profile as long-term supported fallback paths.

hard_constraints.title: One canonical consumer boundary
hard_constraints.detail: MoerProfiler must eventually parse one canonical packet family into one canonical session store; stage 1 must lock that boundary in writing.

checkpoints.title: Freeze ProfileDump as the only canonical offline and TCP format
checkpoints.problem: The repository currently has two streaming-capable profiler formats and extra offline-only paths. That ambiguity blocks clean ownership and invites duplicate import/export work.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: One written decision exists: ProfileDump packets are the only canonical profiler transport and storage format.
Offline files and TCP transport use the same schema+record packet family.
Trace packet transport is explicitly downgraded from target architecture to migration debt.
tasks: Document the accepted packet contract, versioning, and session boundary semantics in one place.
State that CSV and Trace packets are not canonical and will be removed rather than preserved as compatibility paths.
State that any later external exporter is downstream of canonical ProfileDump data rather than a new ingest format.
implementation_notes: ProfileDump packet_version 2 and schema event_type metadata are now part of the canonical contract.
MoerProfiler file and TCP ingest now target ProfileDump packets instead of treating Trace packets as the live consumer contract.

checkpoints.title: Freeze one normalized session and time model
checkpoints.problem: Current profiler code mixes absolute timestamps, per-source generation paths, and unit differences. Any new loader or exporter built on that base will remain wrong.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: All consumer-visible timestamps are session-relative and normalized before UI storage or export logic touches them.
The canonical record contract explicitly states time unit, clock-origin rule, and cross-track ordering expectations.
MoerProfiler is no longer planned around raw producer timestamps being UI-ready values.
tasks: Define one session metadata record that anchors time normalization.
Define how CPU and GPU records are rebased into the same session time domain.
Define the canonical in-memory event fields that MoerProfiler stores after parsing.
implementation_notes: source/profiler/ProfileSession.cpp now owns one explicit normalization boundary: ProfileStore stores only session-relative timestamps and keeps the chosen time_origin_ns in metadata.
Focused tests cover both batch file load normalization and incremental stream normalization where a later packet introduces an earlier event origin.

checkpoints.title: Delete conflicting public transport and offline paths from the target plan
checkpoints.problem: If the plan still treats Trace packet transport, CSV, and source/profile as surviving public paths, every later stage will keep accidental compatibility requirements alive.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: The delete list names Trace packet serialization APIs, CSV import/export, and source/profile as removed-or-reduced migration debt rather than supported architecture.
No later stage assumes continued public support for CSV or Trace packet ingest in MoerProfiler.
No later stage assumes source/profile survives as a separate profiler subsystem.
tasks: List the specific entrypoints and files that lose public architectural status.
State that any surviving helper macro must emit canonical ProfileDump records directly rather than preserve old transport formats.
Keep the deletion plan explicit instead of hiding it behind generic migration wording.
implementation_notes: source/profiler/main.cpp no longer exposes the old CSV load UI or Trace packet live-ingest path as the active consumer workflow.
The old profiler-app-local Trace-shaped consumer data model is gone; the remaining deletion work is repository-wide cleanup of legacy public profiler surfaces and non-canonical Trace transport roles.

checkpoints.title: Freeze the consumer boundary: one parser, one store, one UI data model
checkpoints.problem: MoerProfiler currently parses Trace packets and CSV into a UI-oriented store. That boundary is too early, too format-specific, and too easy to break when new profile kinds arrive.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: MoerProfiler is planned around one canonical parser path that consumes ProfileDump packets only.
The parser produces one consumer-owned session model before any rendering code sees the data.
UI indexing and rendering are downstream of that canonical store rather than mixed into format parsing.
tasks: Define the parser-to-store boundary and its ownership rules.
Define the canonical track, event, and session structures needed by the UI and later exporters.
State that CSV load is removed instead of being kept beside the canonical binary parser.
implementation_notes: A canonical parser path now exists in source/profiler/main.cpp: both TCP and file ingest decode ProfileDump packets and dispatch by schema.event_type.
The boundary now uses dedicated profiler-owned session/event/track structures from source/profiler/ProfileSession.h instead of the old Trace::TraceEvent store.
Normalization now also belongs to that boundary rather than leaking into UI code.

checkpoints.title: Lock the first implementation validation contract
checkpoints.problem: Format migration work is easy to half-land unless the first implementation stage has explicit parser, transport, and producer validation gates.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: The first implementation stage has explicit test coverage targets for file sink parsing, TCP sink parsing, time normalization, and producer record correctness.
Validation uses existing repository scripts only.
No new top-level profiler validation script is introduced.
tasks: Keep parser and transport validation in existing focused tests first.
Run testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 for focused regression whenever ProfileDump parser or producer wiring changes.
Run testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1 after milestone-sized landing steps.
implementation_notes: Focused validation covers ProfileDump file sink, TCP sink, GPU producer integration, profiler file-load normalization, and profiler incremental stream normalization in testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1.
No new top-level validation script was added; the existing focused script remains the first gate.

execution_order: CP-01: freeze the canonical format decision first.
CP-02: freeze the normalized time model before parser or exporter rewrites start.
CP-03: make the delete list explicit so later stages do not reintroduce compatibility debt.
CP-04: lock the consumer-side parser/store/UI boundary.
CP-05: lock the implementation validation contract before M2 starts.
acceptance_criteria: The owning milestone file exists under docs/milestones/profiler and names this stage checkpoint file explicitly.
The stage checkpoint file follows existing repository checkpoint conventions instead of using an ad-hoc loose plan format.
The canonical format, time model, delete list, consumer boundary, and validation contract are all frozen in writing before implementation starts.
validation: Current implementation builds with cmake --build build --config Debug, including MoerProfiler.exe.
Focused regression passed through testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 after the shared ProfileSession module, normalization, and profiler-side ingest tests landed.
Broader regression also passed through testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1 after this landing.
When implementation starts, update this stage checkpoint together with docs/milestones/profiler/format_unification_milestone.json.
Use only existing repository scripts for later validation.
